prompt: A retained event stream receives 2,000 records/s. After a 30-minute dependency outage, the consumer group can complete 2,600 effects/s in aggregate. One partition receives 700 records/s but can complete only 500/s. Retention has four hours remaining for the oldest required input. A poison record is retrying indefinitely on the hot partition, deployments cause frequent rebalances, and management requests a full replay to repair a projection. Produce a safe incident and recovery plan with calculations, ordering, correctness, security and validation.
directAnswer: Declare the incident undrainable as currently shaped despite aggregate spare capacity. The outage backlog is 2,000 x 1,800 = 3,600,000 records. Aggregate spare is 600/s, suggesting an ideal 6,000-second or 100-minute drain, but the hot partition continues to grow by 700 - 500 = 200/s, so no end-to-end drain time exists. Retention remaining is four hours, and investigation plus repair plus a real drain must fit inside it with margin. Contain by pausing the requested replay and deployment churn, protecting the dependency, bounding producer/consumer retries and preserving positions, assignments and event/effect histories. Isolate the poison record under an explicit ordering decision: if later records for the same entity depend on it, quarantine-and-continue can corrupt order, so hold or route that entity until repaired; otherwise quarantine after a bounded attempt budget with full context, owner, alert, retention and controlled redrive. Diagnose the hot partition's key and record distribution. Adding consumers cannot split an exclusively assigned partition. Increase safe partition-local handler/dependency capacity, reduce/admit demand, or redesign the key only with a migration and ordering/merge proof. Stabilize group membership, bound handler/poll time and enforce generation-aware target fencing before resuming rolling changes. Recompute drain with measured per-partition service and require positive spare for every limiting scope. Increase retention only through an approved, capacity-checked change or establish another immutable recovery source; do not reset positions. Plan the projection replay separately after live backlog is safe: exact range, pinned code/config/schema, shadow output, external side effects disabled/idempotently gated, rate below residual live headroom, separate progress, authorization/privacy review, reconciliation and reviewed promotion. Validate oldest age, per-partition lag, poison disposition, one effect per event, no gaps, stable rebalances, replica health, retention margin, dependency SLI, user correctness and exact cleanup.
foundation: Aggregate throughput hides partition-local instability. Backlog drains only when sustainable service exceeds continuing ingress at every required bottleneck. Poison retry, rebalance churn and replay consume the same capacity and can violate order or repeat effects.
reasoningSteps: Calculate outage backlog and ideal aggregate drain.
Show why the hot partition makes the actual drain impossible.
Compare investigation and drain with retention remaining.
Pause replay and membership churn; preserve evidence.
Protect dependency and bound retry/in-flight work.
Classify poison behavior against the ordering invariant.
Bind hottest key and choose safe capacity/demand/key action.
Stabilize assignments and fence stale owners.
Recompute partition-local drain and retention margin from measurements.
Design isolated rate-limited replay and user reconciliation.
seniorAnswer: I reject the tempting 100-minute aggregate answer because one partition grows 200/s. I pause replay and churn, protect the dependency, stop the poison loop under the entity-order contract, and recover positive spare capacity on that partition. I keep positions intact, extend retention only with storage/replica evidence, fence old generations, and make replay a separate shadow change below residual headroom. Recovery is oldest-age and effect correctness, not a green aggregate lag chart.
weakAnswer: We have 600/s spare, so the backlog clears in 100 minutes. Add more consumers, skip the bad message, reset offsets if needed, and start replay now before retention expires.
whyWeak: One partition is undrainable, consumers cannot split it under ordinary exclusive assignment, skipping may corrupt order, reset may lose/repeat work, and replay competes with the already-failing live path.

followUps.prompt: What minimum service rate lets the hot partition clear its own outage backlog in two hours?
followUps.answer: Its 30-minute backlog is 700 x 1,800 = 1,260,000. It needs 175/s spare over two hours, so at least 875/s sustainable service, plus safety margin and any added retry/replay work.

Only after checking storage, replication, disk headroom, deletion/compaction behavior, privacy, cost and whether the change completes before the current horizon. It buys time but does not create drain capacity.

followUps.prompt: When may later records pass a poison event?
followUps.answer: Only when the ordering/invariant contract permits independent progress or the consumer can isolate by entity with a correct reconciliation path. Partition order alone is not the business decision.

followUps.prompt: How much replay rate is safe?
followUps.answer: Only the rate below measured spare capacity after live recovery, dependency headroom, broker disk/network and partition ceilings are reserved; there is no universal percentage.
